title: Why is being scared so fun? - Margee Kerr
speaker: TED-Ed
zh: 【TED-Ed】為什麼害怕這麼有趣？ - 瑪姬·克爾（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Somewhere right now, people are lining up to scare themselves,
cues.en: Somewhere right now, people are lining up to scare themselves,
cues.zh: 現在某處，人們正排著隊來嚇唬自己

cues.text: maybe with a thrill ride or horror movie.
cues.en: maybe with a thrill ride or horror movie.
cues.zh: 現在某處，人們正排著隊來嚇唬自己 也許是玩驚險遊戲或看恐怖電影

cues.text: In fact, in October of 2015 alone, about 28 million people visited a haunted house in the U.S.
cues.en: In fact, in October of 2015 alone, about 28 million people visited a haunted house in the U.S.
cues.zh: 也許是玩驚險遊戲或看恐怖電影 事實上，僅僅在 2015 年 10 月 美國就有約 2800 萬人玩過鬼屋

cues.text: But many consider this behavior perplexing, asking the question,
cues.en: But many consider this behavior perplexing, asking the question,
cues.zh: 但許多人認為這種行為令人費解 而問這個問題 被嚇有什麼好玩的？

cues.text: "What could possibly be fun about being scared?"
cues.en: "What could possibly be fun about being scared?"
cues.zh: 被嚇有什麼好玩的？ 恐懼這個詞名聲並不好 但它並不全是壞事

cues.text: Fear has a bad rap, but it's not all bad.
cues.en: Fear has a bad rap, but it's not all bad.
cues.zh: 恐懼這個詞名聲並不好 但它並不全是壞事 對於初體驗者，恐懼的感覺還不錯

cues.text: For starters, fear can actually feel pretty good.
cues.en: For starters, fear can actually feel pretty good.
cues.zh: 對於初體驗者，恐懼的感覺還不錯

cues.text: When a threat triggers our fight or flight response, our bodies prepare for danger
cues.en: When a threat triggers our fight or flight response, our bodies prepare for danger
cues.zh: 對於初體驗者，恐懼的感覺還不錯 當威脅觸發了我們戰鬥或逃跑的反應 我們的身體準備好要面對危險

cues.text: by releasing chemicals that change how our brains and bodies function.
cues.en: by releasing chemicals that change how our brains and bodies function.
cues.zh: 我們的身體準備好要面對危險 透過釋放化學物質 改變我們大腦和身體的運作

cues.text: This automatic response jumpstarts systems that can aid in survival.
cues.en: This automatic response jumpstarts systems that can aid in survival.
cues.zh: 透過釋放化學物質 改變我們大腦和身體的運作 這套快速反應系統能夠幫助我們生存

cues.text: They do this by making sure we have enough energy and are protected from feeling pain,
cues.en: They do this by making sure we have enough energy and are protected from feeling pain,
cues.zh: 這套快速反應系統能夠幫助我們生存 它們透過到這一點 確保我們有足夠的能量 並免受疼痛的感覺

cues.text: while shutting down nonessential systems, like critical thought.
cues.en: while shutting down nonessential systems, like critical thought.
cues.zh: 並免受疼痛的感覺 同時關閉不必要的系統 像批判性思想

cues.text: Feeling pain-free and energized, while not getting caught up in worrisome thoughts that normally occupy our brains,
cues.en: Feeling pain-free and energized, while not getting caught up in worrisome thoughts that normally occupy our brains,
cues.zh: 同時關閉不必要的系統 像批判性思想 感覺有活力而無痛 不會陷入令人擔憂的狀態 這種通常佔據我們大腦的思想

cues.text: that all sounds great, and it can be because this response is similar, though not exactly the same
cues.en: that all sounds great, and it can be because this response is similar, though not exactly the same
cues.zh: 聽起來還不錯 而且是有可能的 因為恐懼刺激產生的情緒和感受

cues.text: to what we experience in positive, high-arousal states,
cues.en: to what we experience in positive, high-arousal states,
cues.zh: 因為恐懼刺激產生的情緒和感受 與那些常見的正向高度激發 情緒反應大同小異 比如激動、高興甚至性行為

cues.text: like excitement, happiness, and even during sex.
cues.en: like excitement, happiness, and even during sex.
cues.zh: 比如激動、高興甚至性行為 它們的區別就在於處境不同

cues.text: The difference lays in the context.
cues.en: The difference lays in the context.
cues.zh: 它們的區別就在於處境不同 當我們身處險境 我們更注重生存，而不是享受

cues.text: If we're in real danger, we're focused on survival, not fun.
cues.en: If we're in real danger, we're focused on survival, not fun.
cues.zh: 當我們身處險境 我們更注重生存，而不是享受 但是當我們在安全的環境中 嘗試這種高激發情緒時

cues.text: But when we trigger this high arousal response in a safe place,
cues.en: But when we trigger this high arousal response in a safe place,
cues.zh: 但是當我們在安全的環境中 嘗試這種高激發情緒時

cues.text: we can switch over to enjoying the natural high of being scared.
cues.en: we can switch over to enjoying the natural high of being scared.
cues.zh: 但是當我們在安全的環境中 嘗試這種高激發情緒時 我們就可以轉而去享受 這種恐懼帶來的高度興奮了 這就是為什麼人們在雲霄飛車 可以很快從尖叫轉變成笑

cues.text: It's why people on roller coasters can go from screaming to laughing within moments.
cues.en: It's why people on roller coasters can go from screaming to laughing within moments.
cues.zh: 這就是為什麼人們在雲霄飛車 可以很快從尖叫轉變成笑 你的身體已經處於亢奮狀態

cues.text: Your body is already in a euphoric state.
cues.en: Your body is already in a euphoric state.
cues.zh: 你的身體已經處於亢奮狀態 你只是重新標記這個經歷

cues.text: You're just relabeling the experience.
cues.en: You're just relabeling the experience.
cues.zh: 你只是重新標記這個經歷 雖然威脅的反應是普遍的

cues.text: And though the threat response is universal, research shows differences between individuals
cues.en: And though the threat response is universal, research shows differences between individuals
cues.zh: 雖然威脅的反應是普遍的 研究表現出個體之間的差異 以及相關化學物質如何影響其功能

cues.text: in how the chemicals associated with the threat response work.
cues.en: in how the chemicals associated with the threat response work.
cues.zh: 研究表現出個體之間的差異 以及相關化學物質如何影響其功能

cues.text: This explains why some are more prone to thrill-seeking than others.
cues.en: This explains why some are more prone to thrill-seeking than others.
cues.zh: 這就解釋了為什麼有些人 比其他人更喜歡尋求刺激

cues.text: Other normal physical differences explain why some may love the dizziness associated with a loop-de-loop,
cues.en: Other normal physical differences explain why some may love the dizziness associated with a loop-de-loop,
cues.zh: 這就解釋了為什麼有些人 比其他人更喜歡尋求刺激 其他體質的差異說明 為什麼有些人可能喜歡 轉圈圈造成的頭暈

cues.text: while loathing the stomach-drop sensation of a steep roller coaster,
cues.en: while loathing the stomach-drop sensation of a steep roller coaster,
cues.zh: 為什麼有些人可能喜歡 轉圈圈造成的頭暈 而憎恨陡降的雲霄飛車 讓心臟都要跳出來的感覺

cues.text: or why some squeal with delight inside a haunted house, but retreat in terror if taken to an actual cemetery.
cues.en: or why some squeal with delight inside a haunted house, but retreat in terror if taken to an actual cemetery.
cues.zh: 或者為什麼一些人 喜歡在鬼屋裡面尖叫 但去真正的墓地會嚇得逃跑

cues.text: Fear brings more than just a fun, natural high.
cues.en: Fear brings more than just a fun, natural high.
cues.zh: 恐懼帶來的不僅僅是 好玩、自然的興奮感

cues.text: Doing things that we're afraid of can give us a nice boost of self-esteem.
cues.en: Doing things that we're afraid of can give us a nice boost of self-esteem.
cues.zh: 恐懼帶來的不僅僅是 好玩、自然的興奮感 做我們害怕的事情 可以給我們的自尊加把勁 像任何挑戰一樣

cues.text: Like any personal challenge, whether it's running a race or finishing a long book,
cues.en: Like any personal challenge, whether it's running a race or finishing a long book,
cues.zh: 像任何挑戰一樣 不管是賽跑 或是讀完一本很厚的書

cues.text: when we make it through to the end, we feel a sense of accomplishment.
cues.en: when we make it through to the end, we feel a sense of accomplishment.
cues.zh: 當我們把它完成 我們就覺得有成就感

cues.text: This is true even if we know we're not really in any danger.
cues.en: This is true even if we know we're not really in any danger.
cues.zh: 我們就覺得有成就感 這是真實的，即使我們知道 我們沒有處在任何危險中

cues.text: Our thinking brains may know the zombies aren't real, but our bodies tell us otherwise.
cues.en: Our thinking brains may know the zombies aren't real, but our bodies tell us otherwise.
cues.zh: 我們的大腦可能知道殭屍不是真實的 但我們的身體卻不這麼反應 這種恐懼的感覺是真實的

cues.text: The fear feels real, so when we make it through alive,
cues.en: The fear feels real, so when we make it through alive,
cues.zh: 這種恐懼的感覺是真實的 所以，當我們能活著出來 所感受到的滿意度 和成就感也是真實的

cues.text: the satisfaction and sense of accomplishment also feel real.
cues.en: the satisfaction and sense of accomplishment also feel real.
cues.zh: 所感受到的滿意度 和成就感也是真實的

cues.text: This is a great evolutionary adaptation.
cues.en: This is a great evolutionary adaptation.
cues.zh: 所感受到的滿意度 和成就感也是真實的 這是為了適應所進行的偉大進化 那些在勇敢和機智 得到正確平衡的人

cues.text: Those who had the right balance of bravery and wit to know when to push through the fear and when to retreat
cues.en: Those who had the right balance of bravery and wit to know when to push through the fear and when to retreat
cues.zh: 那些在勇敢和機智 得到正確平衡的人 知道什麼時候要克服恐懼或撤退 使其生存下來

cues.text: were rewarded with survival, new food, and new lands.
cues.en: were rewarded with survival, new food, and new lands.
cues.zh: 使其生存下來 得到新的食物 或新的地方

cues.text: Finally, fear can bring people together.
cues.en: Finally, fear can bring people together.
cues.zh: 最後，恐懼可以把人們團結在一起

cues.text: Emotions can be contagious, and when you see your friend scream and laugh,
cues.en: Emotions can be contagious, and when you see your friend scream and laugh,
cues.zh: 最後，恐懼可以把人們團結在一起 情緒是可以傳染的 當你看到你的朋友尖叫或大笑時

cues.text: you feel compelled to do the same.
cues.en: you feel compelled to do the same.
cues.zh: 當你看到你的朋友尖叫或大笑時 你會覺得你必須與他做相同的反應

cues.text: This is because we make sense of what our friends are experiencing by recreating the experience ourselves.
cues.en: This is because we make sense of what our friends are experiencing by recreating the experience ourselves.
cues.zh: 這是因為我們瞭解 我們的朋友正在經歷什麼 因為自己也在體驗一樣的經驗 事實上，你的朋友尖叫時 大腦活躍的部分

cues.text: In fact, the parts of the brain that are active when our friend screams
cues.en: In fact, the parts of the brain that are active when our friend screams
cues.zh: 因為自己也在體驗一樣的經驗 事實上，你的朋友尖叫時 大腦活躍的部分

cues.text: are active in us when we watch them.
cues.en: are active in us when we watch them.
cues.zh: 事實上，你的朋友尖叫時 大腦活躍的部分 在我們看著他們的時候也同時被激發

cues.text: This not only intensifies our own emotional experience, but makes us feel closer to those we're with.
cues.en: This not only intensifies our own emotional experience, but makes us feel closer to those we're with.
cues.zh: 這不僅加劇你自己的情感體驗 也讓我們感覺更接近他們了 這種感覺就跟害怕時一樣

cues.text: The feeling of closeness during times of fear is aided by the hormone oxytocin released during fight or flight.
cues.en: The feeling of closeness during times of fear is aided by the hormone oxytocin released during fight or flight.
cues.zh: 這種感覺就跟害怕時一樣 由激素催產素輔助 戰鬥或逃跑過程中釋放

cues.text: Fear is a powerful emotional experience, and anything that triggers a strong reaction
cues.en: Fear is a powerful emotional experience, and anything that triggers a strong reaction
cues.zh: 由激素催產素輔助 戰鬥或逃跑過程中釋放 恐懼是一種強大的情感體驗 觸發了強烈反響

cues.text: is going to be stored in our memory really well.
cues.en: is going to be stored in our memory really well.
cues.zh: 觸發了強烈反響 將被好好儲存在我們的記憶 你不想忘記有什麼會傷害你

cues.text: You don't want to forget what can hurt you.
cues.en: You don't want to forget what can hurt you.
cues.zh: 你不想忘記有什麼會傷害你 所以，如果你與朋友一起 看恐怖片時是開心的

cues.text: So if your memory of watching a horror film with your friends is positive
cues.en: So if your memory of watching a horror film with your friends is positive
cues.zh: 所以，如果你與朋友一起 看恐怖片時是開心的 並令你留下滿足感

cues.text: and left you with a sense of satisfaction, then you'll want to do it over and over again.
cues.en: and left you with a sense of satisfaction, then you'll want to do it over and over again.
cues.zh: 並令你留下滿足感 那你就想一遍又一遍的這樣做了
